name: David Saldaña
title: Associate Professor; SwarmsLab Director
fitReason: Concrete probabilistic reasoning and human-guided motion learning on compliant aerial hardware, alongside multi-robot autonomy and control.

physicalEvidence.summary: HINT-Blimp (September22,2026) uses a physical SBlimp: Crazyflie2.1 with tilted rotors attached to a helium Mylar balloon. OptiTrack supplies localization, Crazyswarm/Crazyradio transmits velocity commands, and workstation NumPy particle filtering combines pushes with Vosk-decoded speech. Five participants perform300 trials; combined input succeeds86% within at most five interactions. Gesture processing is implemented but not evaluated separately; prior-robustness experiments are simulation. Current SwarmsLab PhD student Subhadeep Koley is first author.
